bug_semantics: SoupServer multi-range handling sorts SoupRange entries with sort_ranges() in soup-message-headers.c, then merges overlapping ranges. The comparator subtracts two goffset (gint64) start values and returns that difference as int. When requested start offsets differ by more than INT_MAX (~2.1e9), truncation flips the comparison sign, violating qsort's ordering contract. The subsequent merge then treats mis-ordered non-overlapping ranges as overlapping and silently drops requested spans from HTTP 206 Partial Content responses on bodies larger than about 2 GB, with no error status.
flaw_origin: The truncation comparator and the post-sort merge were first written together on 2008-10-10 in svn r1181 (git 7aee2eeb). SoupRange.start/end were already goffset, and the tree required GLib/GIO >= 2.15.3 where goffset is gint64, so the 64-to-32 return was a defect at first write rather than a later type widening. git log -L shows the return ra->start - rb->start body unchanged until the 2026 fix.

reasoning: CVE-2026-77014 is a published Red Hat CWE-197 record, not withdrawn or rejected. The mechanism is concrete: sort_ranges() returns a 64-bit SoupRange.start difference as 32-bit int, qsort then mis-orders ranges more than INT_MAX apart, and the merge loop silently omits spans from 206 responses on >~2 GB resources. Issue #519's PoC and the in-tree range-parsing regression ('ranges more than G_MAXINT apart') match that path. Vulnerability-first search (advisory MR !550, issue #519, pickaxe and git log -L on sort_ranges) lands on 7aee2eeb1ca5aaad2162c0fb500a9d9a191a5e27 as the smallest commit that first wrote the comparator and the merge that depends on it. The immediate parent tree still has get_ranges without sort_ranges or the truncated subtraction, so this is a first-write, not a move/refactor/revert. SoupRange was already goffset and GLib/GIO 2.15.3 already defines goffset as gint64, so the truncation existed at introduction. Line history keeps that return statement until e82c13ba, which replaces it with an explicit three-way compare and is therefore both fix_sha and direct_fix_sha; it is a descendant of the BIC and postdates last tagged 3.7.2 while landing on master.
